questions.questionText: The findings of the pilot study were encouraging, and the team is now _____ to a larger trial.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'progressing'. 'Progressing to' means moving forward to the next stage, which follows encouraging results.

questions.questionText: Because the two teams worked in different time zones, they had to _____ their schedules carefully.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'synchronise'. 'Synchronise' means to make things happen at the same time, which distributed teams must do.

questions.questionText: The quality head insisted that every deviation be documented, however _____ it might appear at the time.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'trivial'. 'Trivial' means of little importance; the sentence stresses documenting even unimportant deviations.

questions.questionText: The presentation was so _____ that the client understood the entire architecture in fifteen minutes.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'lucid'. 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, which explains the client's rapid grasp of the architecture.

questions.questionText: The company decided to _____ a part of its profits to employee training.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'allocate'. 'Allocate' means to set aside resources for a particular purpose.

questions.questionText: The firm adopted remote working, which reduced office costs but made informal _____ between colleagues much rarer.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'interaction'. 'Interaction' means communication between people, which remote work reduces.

questions.questionText: The committee asked for additional data before it could _____ the vendor's performance claims.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'validate'. 'Validate' means to confirm that something is accurate, which requires additional data.

questions.questionText: The engineer proposed a _____ solution that could be implemented without replacing the existing infrastructure.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'feasible'. 'Feasible' means practical and capable of being done, which matches a solution that works with existing infrastructure.

questions.questionText: The spare parts were stored in a damp godown, which _____ their useful life considerably.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'shortened'. 'Shortened' means reduced in duration, the effect of dampness on stored components.

questions.questionText: The start-up's first product failed commercially. The founders, instead of giving up, used the experience to _____ a far better second version.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'develop'. 'Develop' means to create and improve something over time, which the founders did next.

questions.questionText: The experiment was repeated with a larger sample so that the earlier result could be either confirmed or _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'refuted'. 'Refuted' means proved wrong, the logical alternative to confirmation.

questions.questionText: The product succeeded in a crowded market mainly because of its _____ pricing.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'competitive'. 'Competitive' pricing means priced attractively in comparison with rivals.

questions.questionText: The forest department launched a drive to _____ degraded land along the river bank.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'restore'. 'Restore' means to bring back to a former condition, which is the aim of treating degraded land.

questions.questionText: The technician asked us to _____ the instrument on a level surface before switching it on.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'lay'. 'Lay' is transitive and takes the object 'the instrument'.

questions.questionText: The bridge was closed for repairs, which caused _____ inconvenience to commuters for nearly a month.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'considerable'. 'Considerable' means great in amount, matching a month-long closure.

questions.questionText: Many first-year students struggle not because the subject is hard but because they lack a study _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'routine'. A 'study routine' is a regular pattern of work, whose absence explains the struggle.

questions.questionText: Before the launch, the marketing team ran a survey to _____ customer expectations.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'gauge'. 'Gauge' means to estimate or judge, which a survey is designed to do.

questions.questionText: Once the safety clearance is received, the contractor may _____ with the excavation work.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'proceed'. 'Proceed with' means to continue or begin an activity after a pause.

questions.questionText: The scheme aims to _____ awareness about water conservation among schoolchildren.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'raise'. The fixed collocation is 'raise awareness'; 'rise' is intransitive and cannot take an object.

questions.questionText: The wetland supports a remarkable variety of plant and animal life, making it a hotspot of _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'biodiversity'. 'Biodiversity' means the variety of living organisms in an area, exactly what the sentence describes.

questions.questionText: The new scheme will come into _____ from the first day of the next financial year.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'effect'. The noun in the fixed phrase 'come into effect' is 'effect', meaning operation or force.

questions.questionText: The training module uses simulations so that trainees can make mistakes without any real-world _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'consequences'. 'Consequences' are the results of an action, and simulation removes real-world costs of error.

questions.questionText: Although the proposal looked attractive on paper, the committee found its assumptions rather _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'optimistic'. 'Optimistic' here means unrealistically hopeful, which explains the committee's reservation.

questions.questionText: The professor's feedback was critical but _____, pointing out exactly how the draft could be improved.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'constructive'. 'Constructive' means helpful and aimed at improvement, which the second clause confirms.

questions.questionText: The training programme was designed to _____ the gap between academic knowledge and industry expectations.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'bridge'. The collocation 'bridge the gap' means to reduce or close a difference between two things.

questions.questionText: After the disappointing results, the coach decided to _____ the training schedule completely.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'overhaul'. 'Overhaul' means to revise thoroughly, which matches the word 'completely'.

questions.questionText: The notice used the word 'immediately' twice, giving the instruction an _____ tone.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'urgent'. 'Urgent' means requiring immediate action, which the repeated word signals.

questions.questionText: The village received a new borewell last year. Unfortunately, the pump has remained _____ for want of a simple spare part.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'idle'. 'Idle' means not in use, which a pump lacking a spare part would be.

questions.questionText: The team's first estimate proved far too low. In the revised plan they added a _____ to absorb unexpected delays.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'buffer'. A 'buffer' is extra allowance built in to absorb variation, here of time.

questions.questionText: The seminar hall was booked for the whole day, so the organisers had to find an _____ venue for the evening quiz.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'alternative'. 'Alternative' means another option available, which a clash of bookings requires.

questions.questionText: Several small suppliers were unable to _____ with the new emission norms and had to shut down.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'comply'. The verb that takes the preposition 'with' in this sense is 'comply'; one complies with a regulation.

questions.questionText: The technician could not _____ the fault because the error message was too vague.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'pinpoint'. 'Pinpoint' means to identify exactly, which a vague error message makes difficult.

questions.questionText: The chief executive struck an _____ note in the annual letter, promising a return to growth.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'upbeat'. 'Upbeat' means cheerful and hopeful, which matches a promise of renewed growth.

questions.questionText: Despite the setback in the first quarter, the chief executive remained _____ about meeting the annual target.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'optimistic'. 'Optimistic' means hopeful about the future; the contrast marker 'despite' signals a positive attitude after a setback.

questions.questionText: The paper was rejected because the methodology section did not _____ how the data had been collected.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'specify'. 'Specify' means to state clearly and in detail, which a methodology section must do.

questions.questionText: The software licence prohibits redistribution, so the college obtained written _____ before sharing the tool with a partner institute.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'permission'. 'Permission' is formal consent, which a restrictive licence makes necessary.

questions.questionText: Although the error was _____, it was enough to fail the automated validation check.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'slight'. 'Slight' means small; the contrast with 'enough to fail' shows the error was minor yet decisive.

questions.questionText: The old bridge was declared unsafe, and traffic was _____ to the newly built bypass.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'diverted'. 'Diverted' means redirected along another route, which is what happens when a bridge is closed.

questions.questionText: The supervisor refused to _____ repeated violations of the safety protocol, however minor they seemed.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'condone'. 'Condone' means to accept or overlook wrong behaviour; the supervisor would not overlook the violations.

questions.questionText: Several passengers complained that the announcement was barely _____ over the station's loudspeakers.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'audible'. 'Audible' means able to be heard, which is the relevant quality for an announcement.

questions.questionText: Young engineers are advised to _____ feedback rather than wait for the annual review.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'solicit'. 'Solicit' means to ask for something actively, which the sentence contrasts with waiting.

questions.questionText: As the deadline approached, the team had to _____ which defects to fix first.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'prioritise'. 'Prioritise' means to decide the order of importance, which is required when time is short.

questions.questionText: The team's documentation was praised for anticipating the questions a new maintainer would be likely to _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'raise'. 'Raise a question' is the standard collocation; 'rise' cannot take an object.

questions.questionText: Regular backups _____ that no more than a day's work can ever be lost.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'ensure'. 'Ensure' means to make certain that something happens; 'insure' relates to insurance cover.

questions.questionText: The team repeated the measurement several times to rule out any _____ error in the instrument.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'systematic'. 'Systematic error' is a consistent bias in measurement, which repetition and calibration help detect.

questions.questionText: The team meets every Monday to _____ progress and decide the week's priorities.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'review'. 'Review' means to examine something again in order to assess it, the purpose of such meetings.

questions.questionText: The study's conclusions must be treated with care because the sample was not _____ of the whole population.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'representative'. 'Representative' means typical of a larger group, and an unrepresentative sample limits conclusions.

questions.questionText: The colour of the new packaging was chosen to _____ the company's existing brand identity.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'complement'. 'Complement' means to combine well with something; 'compliment' means to praise.

questions.questionText: The firm's success is largely _____ to its willingness to invest in research during lean years.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'attributable'. 'Attributable to' means caused by or resulting from something.

questions.questionText: The meeting was shifted to a _____ hour so that the overseas team could join.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'later'. 'Later' means further on in time, which is the sense needed for rescheduling.

questions.questionText: Automation has made the assembly line far more efficient, but it has also made certain manual skills _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'redundant'. 'Redundant' means no longer needed, which is the natural consequence of automation for manual skills.

questions.questionText: The organisation provides a small grant so that promising ideas can be tested before seeking _____ funding.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'larger'. 'Larger' contrasts the small initial grant with the bigger sums sought later.

questions.questionText: The project failed to take off because the responsibilities of the two teams were never clearly _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'demarcated'. 'Demarcated' means marked out as separate, and unclear boundaries of responsibility caused the failure.

questions.questionText: Buying in bulk proved more _____ for the hostel mess than purchasing weekly.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'economical'. 'Economical' means avoiding waste of money, which bulk buying achieves.

questions.questionText: The sensor readings were _____ across all three trials, which increased the team's confidence in the design.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'consistent'. 'Consistent' means unchanging and dependable, which is why the readings increased confidence.

questions.questionText: The vehicle remained _____ at the signal for nearly five minutes because of the breakdown ahead.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'stationary'. 'Stationary' means standing still, which describes a vehicle that is not moving.

questions.questionText: Industrial effluents released without treatment continue to _____ the groundwater in the region.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'contaminate'. 'Contaminate' means to make impure by adding harmful substances, which untreated effluents do.

questions.questionText: The new recruit was praised for her _____ attitude; she volunteered for tasks before being asked.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'proactive'. 'Proactive' means acting in anticipation rather than waiting to be told, exactly as described.

questions.questionText: Of the two proposals, the _____ was chosen because it required no additional staff.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'latter'. 'Latter' refers to the second of two things mentioned; 'later' refers to time.

questions.questionText: The sensors are inexpensive; _____, they are accurate enough for most classroom experiments.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'moreover'. 'Moreover' adds a further point in the same direction as the first.

questions.questionText: The new encryption standard was adopted after researchers discovered a serious _____ in the older algorithm.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'vulnerability'. 'Vulnerability' means a weakness that can be exploited, which is why a new standard was needed.

questions.questionText: The workshop concluded with a session on how to _____ constructive feedback to colleagues.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'offer'. 'Offer feedback' means to provide it, which is the usual professional collocation.

questions.questionText: The firm offers flexible hours, which has helped it _____ experienced professionals who value work-life balance.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'attract'. 'Attract' means to draw people in, which flexible hours do for such professionals.

questions.questionText: Public transport in the city improved considerably after the authority began to _____ passenger feedback in its planning.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'incorporate'. 'Incorporate' means to include something as part of a whole, here feedback in planning.

questions.questionText: Because the backup had never been tested, the recovery process proved far more _____ than expected.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'cumbersome'. 'Cumbersome' means slow and difficult to manage, which an untested backup process is likely to be.

questions.questionText: Since the budget was fixed, the design team had to work within tight _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'constraints'. 'Constraints' are limitations, which a fixed budget imposes on design choices.

questions.questionText: The researcher formulated a clear _____ and then designed an experiment to test it.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'hypothesis'. 'Hypothesis' is a proposed explanation that an experiment is designed to test.

questions.questionText: The committee thanked the outgoing secretary for the _____ with which she had maintained the accounts.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'diligence'. 'Diligence' means careful and persistent effort, which good record-keeping demonstrates.

questions.questionText: The city's waste policy is not _____ in the long run, as landfill space will be exhausted within a decade.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'sustainable'. 'Sustainable' means able to be maintained over time, which the policy is not if space runs out.

questions.questionText: Because the components came from three different suppliers, the assembly team spent considerable time ensuring that the tolerances _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'matched'. 'Matched' means agreed with one another, which is necessary for parts from different sources.

questions.questionText: The negotiation finally reached an impasse, and the matter was referred to an independent _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'arbitrator'. An 'arbitrator' is a neutral third party appointed to settle a dispute.

questions.questionText: Heavy rainfall during the harvest season can _____ the quality of the stored grain.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'impair'. 'Impair' means to weaken or damage, the likely effect of moisture on stored grain.

questions.questionText: The report must be submitted by Friday; the committee cannot _____ any further delay.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'accommodate'. 'Accommodate' here means to allow room for something, which the committee cannot do.

questions.questionText: The supervisor's remarks were meant to encourage, not to _____, the junior engineers.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'demoralise'. 'Demoralise' means to destroy confidence, the natural opposite of 'encourage' in this contrast.

questions.questionText: The reviewer asked the authors to _____ their claim that the model works for all input sizes.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'qualify'. To 'qualify' a claim is to limit it so that it is not overstated, which a sweeping claim requires.

questions.questionText: The security team managed to _____ the intrusion before any data left the network.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'contain'. 'Contain' means to prevent something from spreading, which stopped the breach from causing loss.

questions.questionText: The company decided to _____ its expansion plans because the economic outlook had become uncertain.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'postpone'. 'Postpone' means to delay something to a later time, which is what an uncertain economic outlook would prompt.

questions.questionText: The two departments agreed to share the laboratory, which proved _____ to both in terms of cost.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'advantageous'. 'Advantageous' means beneficial, which sharing costs clearly is.

questions.questionText: Faced with conflicting reports, the committee was _____ about drawing any firm conclusion.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'hesitant'. 'Hesitant' means reluctant to act, which conflicting evidence naturally produces.

questions.questionText: The project ran smoothly in the first phase; _____, several problems appeared once the field trials began.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'however'. 'However' marks the contrast between a smooth first phase and later problems.

questions.questionText: The team leader asked the members to _____ the tasks among themselves so that no one was overloaded.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'distribute'. 'Distribute' means to share out among several people, which prevents any single member from being overloaded.

questions.questionText: The research findings were considered _____ because the sample size was far too small.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'inconclusive'. 'Inconclusive' means not leading to a firm conclusion, which a very small sample would cause.

questions.questionText: The new employee was advised to _____ to the organisation's working style before suggesting changes.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'adapt'. 'Adapt' means to adjust oneself to new conditions; 'adopt' means to take something up.

questions.questionText: The board asked the committee to _____ the recommendation only after the cost had been verified.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'accept'. 'Accept' means to agree to something, which is what a board does with a recommendation.

questions.questionText: Instead of blaming the vendor, the project manager chose to _____ responsibility for the delay.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'assume'. 'Assume responsibility' means to take it upon oneself, which contrasts with blaming someone else.

questions.questionText: The counsellor advised the student to choose a specialisation that matched her _____ rather than current job trends.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'aptitude'. 'Aptitude' means natural ability for something, which is the sensible basis for choosing a field.

questions.questionText: The convocation address was delivered by an _____ scientist who had led the lunar mission.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'eminent'. 'Eminent' means famous and respected, which fits a distinguished scientist.

questions.questionText: The committee's decision was unanimous: not a single member _____ to the proposal.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'objected'. 'Objected' means expressed opposition, and its absence is what makes a decision unanimous.

questions.questionText: The new intern was nervous at first but soon became _____ with the testing procedure.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'familiar'. 'Familiar with' means having good knowledge of something through experience.

questions.questionText: He joined the start-up for the experience, not for the salary, which was fairly _____ at the time.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'modest'. 'Modest' means small in amount, which explains why salary was not his motive.

questions.questionText: The company purchased a four-acre _____ on the outskirts for its new campus.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'site'. 'Site' means a plot of land or location, which is what the company bought.

questions.questionText: Because attendance was poor, the department decided to _____ the elective in the coming semester.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'discontinue'. 'Discontinue' means to stop offering something, the natural response to poor attendance.

questions.questionText: The committee rejected the first design on the ground that it was _____ to the user's actual needs.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'irrelevant'. 'Irrelevant' means not connected with the matter in hand, here the real needs of users.

questions.questionText: Because the proposal involved public money, the committee insisted on a fully _____ selection process.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'transparent'. 'Transparent' means open to scrutiny, which public funds demand.

questions.questionText: The panel asked the student to _____ between correlation and causation with an example.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'distinguish'. 'Distinguish between' means to point out the difference between two things.

questions.questionText: After three rounds of interviews, the panel found the candidates so evenly matched that the final choice was _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'difficult'. 'Difficult' follows from candidates being evenly matched.

questions.questionText: The speaker's tone was so _____ that even those who disagreed listened without interrupting.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'measured'. 'Measured' means calm and carefully controlled, which explains the respectful hearing.

questions.questionText: The college canteen switched to steel plates in order to _____ the use of disposable plastic.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'curb'. 'Curb' means to restrain or reduce, which the switch is intended to do.

questions.questionText: From the repeated delays, the client began to _____ that the vendor lacked the capacity to deliver.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'infer'. To 'infer' is to reach a conclusion from evidence, which the client does here.

questions.questionText: The monument is of great _____ importance and attracts researchers from many countries.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'historical'. 'Historical' means relating to the study of the past; 'historic' means famous in history.

questions.questionText: The institute invited alumni to mentor final-year students. The response was so warm that the programme is now a _____ feature of the academic calendar.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'regular'. 'Regular' means recurring at fixed intervals, which a warmly received programme becomes.

questions.questionText: The organisation provides counselling so that employees under stress can seek help without any _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'stigma'. 'Stigma' means social disapproval, which confidential counselling aims to remove.

questions.questionText: The firm decided to _____ part of its software testing to a specialised vendor in order to save time.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'outsource'. 'Outsource' means to contract work out to an external organisation, which is what hiring a vendor means.

questions.questionText: The senior architect reviewed the code and found the structure sound, though the naming conventions were _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'inconsistent'. 'Inconsistent' means not uniform, a common criticism of naming conventions in code reviews.

questions.questionText: The internal audit found that the approval process was unnecessarily long. The management therefore decided to _____ it by removing two redundant steps.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'streamline'. 'Streamline' means to make a process simpler and more efficient, which removing redundant steps achieves.

questions.questionText: The negotiation stalled because neither side was prepared to _____ on the delivery schedule.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'budge'. To 'budge' is to change one's position slightly; refusing to budge means the talks stall.

questions.questionText: The intern was asked to _____ the minutes of the meeting and circulate them by evening.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'draft'. 'Draft' means to prepare a first written version of a document.

questions.questionText: The workshop aims to help students _____ the confidence needed to speak in public.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'build'. The collocation 'build confidence' means to develop it gradually.

questions.questionText: Solar and wind power are described as _____ sources because they are naturally replenished.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'renewable'. 'Renewable' refers to resources that are naturally replaced, as the explanation in the sentence shows.

questions.questionText: Since the data set contained several missing values, the analyst had to _____ the results with care.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'interpret'. 'Interpret' means to explain the meaning of something; missing values demand careful interpretation.

questions.questionText: The two data sets showed a strong _____, although the analyst was careful not to claim causation.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'correlation'. 'Correlation' describes a statistical relationship between variables, which is distinct from causation.

questions.questionText: The audit noted a _____ rise in travel expenses, from four lakh rupees to nearly eleven lakh.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'substantial'. 'Substantial' means large in amount, which the figures in the sentence confirm.

questions.questionText: The handbook advises engineers to keep a record of every design change, however small, to maintain _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'traceability'. 'Traceability' means the ability to track the history of changes, which such records provide.

questions.questionText: The signing of the peace agreement was described as a _____ moment for the region.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'historic'. 'Historic' means momentous and likely to be remembered in history.

questions.questionText: The sensor network failed during the storm because the nodes had not been designed to _____ such extreme conditions.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'withstand'. 'Withstand' means to endure without damage, which the nodes could not do.

questions.questionText: The chief engineer insisted that every assumption in the model be stated _____ so that reviewers could test it.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'explicitly'. 'Explicitly' means stated openly and clearly, which allows reviewers to check assumptions.

questions.questionText: The library has started a digital archive so that rare manuscripts can be studied without being _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'handled'. 'Handled' means touched physically, which digitisation is intended to avoid for fragile manuscripts.

questions.questionText: The young officer listened _____ while the veteran engineer explained the failure analysis.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'respectfully'. 'Respectfully' describes the manner of listening, showing deference.

questions.questionText: The auditors asked the firm to _____ the discrepancy between the stock register and the physical count.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reconcile'. 'Reconcile' means to make two sets of figures agree, which is standard audit vocabulary.

questions.questionText: The supervisor asked the team to _____ the earlier estimate in the light of the new requirements.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'revise'. 'Revise' means to change something after reconsideration, which new requirements demand.

questions.questionText: The manual warns that using a non-standard charger may _____ the warranty on the device.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'void'. To 'void' a warranty means to make it invalid, the standard legal usage.

questions.questionText: The appraisal system was redesigned to reward _____ rather than merely long service.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'merit'. 'Merit' means demonstrated ability and achievement, which the sentence contrasts with length of service.

questions.questionText: The two teams were working on very similar features without knowing it, a clear sign of poor internal _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'communication'. 'Communication' failure explains why two teams duplicated effort unknowingly.

questions.questionText: The investigators found no evidence of tampering, so they concluded that the failure was purely _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'accidental'. 'Accidental' means unintentional, which follows logically from the absence of tampering.

questions.questionText: Since none of the team members had worked on embedded systems before, the project involved a steep learning _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'curve'. The idiom 'steep learning curve' describes a situation requiring rapid acquisition of new skills.

questions.questionText: Because he had no formal training, he learnt the software by _____ and error.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'trial'. The idiom 'trial and error' means learning by trying and correcting mistakes.

questions.questionText: Fuel prices rose only _____ last month, so transporters did not revise their rates.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'marginally'. 'Marginally' means by a very small amount, which explains why rates were unchanged.

questions.questionText: All the delegates attended the valedictory session _____ two who had an early flight.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'except'. 'Except' means apart from; 'accept' means to receive willingly.

questions.questionText: Engineers were asked to _____ the three competing designs against cost, weight and reliability.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'evaluate'. 'Evaluate' means to judge the value of something against criteria.

questions.questionText: The volunteer's _____ efforts during the flood relief work were acknowledged by the district administration.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'tireless'. 'Tireless' means showing great effort without becoming weary, which is why the efforts were praised.

questions.questionText: The client wanted the dashboard ready in a week, but the developers felt that the timeline was wholly _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unrealistic'. 'Unrealistic' means not achievable in practice, which is the developers' objection to the deadline.

questions.questionText: The scheme failed because it was designed centrally without taking local conditions into _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'account'. The idiom 'take into account' means to consider; ignoring local conditions caused failure.

questions.questionText: The proposal was rejected not because it lacked merit but because the cost estimate was considered _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'prohibitive'. 'Prohibitive' describes a cost so high that it prevents something from being done.

questions.questionText: The company introduced flexible seating, but many employees found the constant change of desks _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'disruptive'. 'Disruptive' means causing disturbance to normal working, the common complaint about hot-desking.

questions.questionText: She was selected for the role _____ of her experience with distributed systems.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'because'. 'Because of' states the reason for her selection, which her experience provides.

questions.questionText: The storeroom had run out of _____, so the office could not print the certificates.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'stationery'. 'Stationery' refers to writing materials; 'stationary' means not moving.

questions.questionText: The firm lost the tender because its bid, though technically strong, was not _____ competitive.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'commercially'. 'Commercially' refers to price and business terms, which the technical strength could not offset.

questions.questionText: The pandemic caused an _____ slowdown that affected employment across several sectors.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'economic'. 'Economic' relates to the economy as a whole, which is the sense required here.

questions.questionText: The scheme was introduced in three districts on a _____ basis before being extended statewide.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'pilot'. A 'pilot' basis means a small trial carried out before full implementation.

questions.questionText: Employees were told not to use office computers for _____ work during peak hours.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'personal'. 'Personal' means relating to one's private life, which is what the restriction concerns.

questions.questionText: The software performed well in controlled testing. However, its behaviour became _____ when it was exposed to unpredictable network conditions.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unstable'. 'Unstable' means liable to change unpredictably, which contrasts with the steady performance seen in controlled testing.

questions.questionText: The consultant's recommendations were sound but too _____ for a firm with only twelve employees.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'elaborate'. 'Elaborate' means complicated and detailed, which would overburden a very small firm.

questions.questionText: Many traditional industries have had to _____ digital tools in order to stay in business.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'adopt'. 'Adopt' means to take something up and start using it, while 'adapt' means to modify oneself.

questions.questionText: Costs are expected to _____ sharply once the new tariff comes into force.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'rise'. 'Rise' is intransitive and takes no object; 'raise' needs a direct object.

questions.questionText: The organisation adopted a zero-tolerance policy because earlier warnings had failed to _____ misconduct.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'deter'. 'Deter' means to discourage by fear of consequences; 'defer' means to postpone.

questions.questionText: The cost of the solar installation will be _____ by the savings on electricity within four years.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'offset'. 'Offset' means balanced out by something of equal value, here future savings.

questions.questionText: The letter was polite but firm, making the company's position on the refund perfectly _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'clear'. 'Clear' means easily understood, which a firm letter is intended to make the position.

questions.questionText: The team adopted an agile approach so that it could respond _____ to changing requirements.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'swiftly'. 'Swiftly' means quickly, which is the main advantage claimed for agile methods.

questions.questionText: The findings are based on _____ observation rather than on theoretical reasoning alone.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'empirical'. 'Empirical' means based on observation or experience, which the sentence contrasts with theory.

questions.questionText: Because the two readings were taken under different conditions, the comparison between them is not strictly _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'valid'. 'Valid' means logically sound; differing conditions undermine the comparison.

questions.questionText: The policy requires that all contractors _____ to the same safety standards as regular employees.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'adhere'. 'Adhere to' means to follow a rule or standard closely.

questions.questionText: The driver was praised for being _____ enough to notice the loose bolt before the trip.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'conscientious'. 'Conscientious' means careful and thorough in one's duties.

questions.questionText: The machine stopped automatically, which suggests that the safety interlock worked as _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'intended'. 'As intended' means in the manner planned by the designers, which a correct automatic stop shows.

questions.questionText: The supervisor's role is to _____ work, not to perform every task personally.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'delegate'. 'Delegate' means to assign tasks to others, which is contrasted with doing everything oneself.

questions.questionText: The company issued a public apology, which did much to _____ the damage to its reputation.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'limit'. 'Limit' means to keep within bounds, the purpose of a prompt public apology.

questions.questionText: The mentor encouraged her to view the rejection as a temporary _____ rather than a final verdict.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'setback'. 'Setback' means a reversal of progress, which the word 'temporary' supports.

questions.questionText: Unlike the earlier model, which needed a technician for installation, the new unit can be set up by the user _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unaided'. 'Unaided' means without help, which contrasts with needing a technician.

questions.questionText: His explanation was plausible, yet the panel remained _____ until the logs were produced.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'sceptical'. 'Sceptical' means doubtful, which the contrast word 'yet' signals despite a plausible story.

questions.questionText: The unused cables continued to _____ in the corner of the laboratory for months.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'lie'. 'Lie' is intransitive and means to rest in a horizontal position.

questions.questionText: The witness gave a _____ account, supported by timestamps from the security camera.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'credible'. 'Credible' means believable; 'credulous' describes a person who believes things too readily.

questions.questionText: The committee could not agree, so the chairperson suggested a _____ that gave each side part of what it wanted.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'compromise'. A 'compromise' is a settlement in which both parties make concessions.

questions.questionText: The minister laid the foundation stone of the metro extension, which is expected to _____ traffic congestion.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'ease'. 'Ease' means to make less severe, the usual effect of a new metro line on congestion.

questions.questionText: The bank's mobile app was redesigned after users complained about the number of steps needed for a transfer. The new version is noticeably _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'simpler'. 'Simpler' answers the complaint about too many steps.

questions.questionText: The reviewer's comments were blunt, and several authors found them unnecessarily _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'harsh'. 'Harsh' means severe and unkind, which fits comments described as unnecessarily blunt.

questions.questionText: Rather than announcing a complete ban, the authority chose a _____ reduction over five years.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'phased'. 'Phased' means carried out in stages, which contrasts with an immediate ban.

questions.questionText: The negotiation succeeded because both sides were willing to make _____ concessions.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'mutual'. 'Mutual' means shared by both parties, which is what makes a negotiation succeed.

questions.questionText: The start-up could not _____ its best engineers once larger firms began offering far higher salaries.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'retain'. 'Retain' means to keep; the problem described is losing existing employees, not hiring new ones.

questions.questionText: Because the error appeared only once in ten thousand runs, it was extremely difficult to _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reproduce'. 'Reproduce' means to make something happen again, which rare intermittent faults resist.

questions.questionText: A single careless message on social media can seriously _____ a company's reputation.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'damage'. 'Damage' means to harm, which is the risk described.

questions.questionText: The heavy rain did not _____ the turnout at the job fair; nearly two thousand students attended.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'affect'. 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; 'effect' as a noun means a result.

questions.questionText: The firm has consistently _____ its emission targets, reducing carbon output for five successive years.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'met'. 'Met' here means achieved; the second clause shows continued success, not failure.

questions.questionText: The maintenance log had not been updated for months, which made it impossible to establish a reliable service _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'history'. 'Service history' is the record of past maintenance, which the missing log destroys.

questions.questionText: A good mentor does not give ready answers but helps the trainee _____ the problem independently.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'analyse'. 'Analyse' means to examine systematically; the mentor guides the trainee to work through the problem.

questions.questionText: Two independent laboratories were asked to repeat the test in order to establish the _____ of the result.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reliability'. 'Reliability' refers to consistency of results when a test is repeated.

questions.questionText: The author was asked to _____ the original study properly in the reference list.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'cite'. 'Cite' means to quote or refer to a source; 'site' is a place.

questions.questionText: The committee met for three hours but could not _____ a conclusion on the revised fee structure.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reach'. The fixed collocation is 'reach a conclusion', meaning to arrive at a decision after discussion.

questions.questionText: Rather than replacing the entire system, the vendor suggested an _____ upgrade spread over two years.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'incremental'. 'Incremental' means proceeding in small stages, which matches an upgrade spread over two years.

questions.questionText: The recruiter explained that the firm values attitude as much as skill, because technical gaps can usually be _____ through training.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'closed'. The collocation 'close a gap' means to remove the difference, which training does.

questions.questionText: The hostel mess committee invited suggestions from students. Most of the proposals, however, were impractical and only a few were finally _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'implemented'. 'Implemented' means put into practice, which is what happens to the few workable suggestions.

questions.questionText: The laboratory must be kept dust-free; _____, the optical components will need frequent cleaning.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'otherwise'. 'Otherwise' introduces what will happen if the stated condition is not met.

questions.questionText: The professor refused to accept the assignment because large sections had been copied without acknowledgement, which amounts to _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'plagiarism'. 'Plagiarism' is the use of another's work without credit, exactly as described.

questions.questionText: The design review revealed a _____ flaw that could not be corrected by changing a few parameters.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'fundamental'. 'Fundamental' means affecting the basis of something, which is why small changes cannot fix it.

questions.questionText: Although the two algorithms produce the same output, the second is far more memory-_____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'efficient'. 'Memory-efficient' is the standard compound describing low memory consumption.

questions.questionText: Because the matter concerned two partner firms, the mail was worded _____ to avoid giving offence.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'diplomatically'. 'Diplomatically' means tactfully, which is required when writing to sensitive partners.

questions.questionText: The bank introduced two-factor authentication to prevent _____ access to customer accounts.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unauthorised'. 'Unauthorised' means without permission, which is exactly what authentication is designed to prevent.

questions.questionText: The research grant was withdrawn when the committee discovered that the data had been _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'fabricated'. 'Fabricated' means invented dishonestly, a serious offence that justifies withdrawing a grant.

questions.questionText: Although the engine is powerful, it is not very _____, consuming nearly nine litres per hundred kilometres.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'economical'. 'Economical' means giving good value for the resources used; 'economic' relates to the economy as a whole.

questions.questionText: Phishing emails often look genuine, so staff are trained to _____ the sender's address before clicking any link.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'verify'. 'Verify' means to check that something is true, which is the recommended precaution against phishing.

questions.questionText: The laboratory equipment is now almost twenty years old and has become _____ for advanced research.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'obsolete'. 'Obsolete' means out of date and no longer useful, which fits twenty-year-old research equipment.

questions.questionText: The _____ reason for the delay was the late arrival of imported components.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'principal'. 'Principal' here is an adjective meaning main or chief.

questions.questionText: During the interview, the candidate was asked to _____ a situation in which she had resolved a conflict.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'describe'. 'Describe' means to give an account of something, which is what behavioural interview questions ask for.

questions.questionText: The company's revenue has grown steadily, whereas its profit margin has continued to _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'shrink'. 'Whereas' signals contrast with steady growth, so the margin must be getting smaller.

questions.questionText: Although the machine is old, it has been maintained so well that it still works _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'flawlessly'. 'Flawlessly' means without any faults, which good maintenance of an old machine can achieve.

questions.questionText: The report was praised for being _____: it covered every aspect of the problem within ten pages.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'comprehensive'. 'Comprehensive' means complete and covering all aspects, which the second clause confirms.

questions.questionText: The firm's internal survey showed that employees wanted clearer career paths, so the human resources team drew up a detailed _____ framework.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'progression'. 'Progression' refers to advancement through stages, which career paths describe.

questions.questionText: While the northern plants reported record output, the southern units continued to _____ behind their targets.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'lag'. 'Lag behind' means to fall short of a standard, which contrasts with record output.

questions.questionText: The new policy was introduced _____ reduce paperwork and speed up approvals.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'to'. The infinitive of purpose uses 'to', giving the reason for introducing the policy.

questions.questionText: The authors openly discussed the _____ of their study, including the short observation period.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'limitations'. 'Limitations' are the shortcomings of a study, and a short observation period is one such weakness.

questions.questionText: The professor asked the students to _____ their conclusions with evidence from the experiment.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'substantiate'. 'Substantiate' means to support a claim with proof, which matches the demand for evidence.

questions.questionText: The code passed all unit tests, _____ it failed the moment it was integrated with the billing service.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'yet'. 'Yet' signals an unexpected contrast between passing tests and failing on integration.

questions.questionText: The company ran an awareness campaign because many customers were unaware of their right to _____ a defective product.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'return'. 'Return' means to take a product back to the seller, which consumer rights allow.

questions.questionText: Online frauds succeed largely because some users are too _____ to question unusual requests.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'credulous'. 'Credulous' means too ready to believe, which is the weakness exploited by fraudsters.

questions.questionText: The difference between the two measurements was _____, so the engineers treated the readings as identical.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'negligible'. 'Negligible' means too small to matter, which is why the readings were treated as the same.

questions.questionText: The examination tests application rather than recall, so rote learning is of _____ value.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'limited'. 'Limited' means small in extent; if application is tested, memorisation helps only a little.

questions.questionText: The new recruit found the jargon used in meetings quite _____ during his first few weeks.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'bewildering'. 'Bewildering' means confusing, the natural reaction of a newcomer to unfamiliar jargon.

questions.questionText: The engineer's calculations were correct, but his presentation lacked _____, so the committee asked for a rewrite.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'clarity'. 'Clarity' means clearness of expression, which the committee found missing.

questions.questionText: The manager's calm response helped to _____ a tense situation during the client review.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'defuse'. To 'defuse' a situation is to reduce its tension; 'diffuse' means to spread out.

questions.questionText: The customer care executive was praised for handling an angry caller with remarkable _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'tact'. 'Tact' means sensitivity in dealing with difficult situations or people.

questions.questionText: The two candidates were ranked first and second, and the prizes were given to them _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'respectively'. 'Respectively' means in the order already mentioned; 'respectfully' means with respect.

questions.questionText: The patient's condition was described as _____, and he was shifted to intensive care immediately.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'critical'. 'Critical' means extremely serious, consistent with an immediate shift to intensive care.

questions.questionText: The company deployed an intrusion detection system to _____ unusual activity in real time.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'flag'. 'Flag' means to mark something for attention, which is what a detection system does with anomalies.

questions.questionText: The interviewer noted that the candidate could _____ complex ideas in simple language.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'articulate'. 'Articulate' means to express clearly, which is the skill being praised.

questions.questionText: In her appraisal, the manager described the trainee's progress as steady and her attitude as _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'commendable'. 'Commendable' means deserving praise, which fits a positive appraisal.

questions.questionText: The new regulation applies to all vehicles _____ of their date of registration.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'irrespective'. The fixed phrase is 'irrespective of', meaning without regard to.

questions.questionText: During the power cut, the data centre switched to its backup generators within seconds. The outage therefore went almost _____ by customers.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unnoticed'. 'Unnoticed' means not observed, which a seconds-long switchover would make the outage.

questions.questionText: The chairperson summed up the discussion and asked the members to _____ on the two shortlisted options.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'vote'. 'Vote on' means to decide by casting votes, the usual way of choosing between shortlisted options.

questions.questionText: Although the prototype was inexpensive to build, its design was not sufficiently _____ for large-scale deployment.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'robust'. 'Robust' means strong and able to withstand demanding conditions, which large-scale deployment requires.

questions.questionText: Because the road was flooded, several students were unable to _____ the examination centre on time.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reach'. 'Reach' means to arrive at a place; the flooded road prevented the students from arriving.

questions.questionText: A project of this size requires close _____ between design, procurement and production teams.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'coordination'. 'Coordination' means organised cooperation among different groups.

questions.questionText: The vendor missed three consecutive deadlines; _____, the contract was terminated.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'consequently'. 'Consequently' introduces a result, which termination is after repeated failures.

questions.questionText: His argument was logically sound, although the evidence he cited was somewhat _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'dated'. 'Dated' means out of date, which 'although' signals as a weakness alongside sound logic.

questions.questionText: The machine's performance deteriorated gradually rather than failing suddenly, which made the fault hard to _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'detect'. 'Detect' means to discover the presence of something, which gradual deterioration makes difficult.

questions.questionText: Employees were reminded that customer data is strictly _____ and must not be shared outside the team.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'confidential'. 'Confidential' means intended to be kept secret, which is why sharing is prohibited.

questions.questionText: Because the data were sensitive, access was _____ to three senior analysts.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'restricted'. 'Restricted' means limited, which protecting sensitive data requires.

questions.questionText: The union asked the management to _____ the daily wage of contract workers.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'raise'. 'Raise' is transitive and takes the object 'the daily wage'.

questions.questionText: The laboratory results differed from the field results, a discrepancy the team could not easily _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'explain'. 'Explain' means to give a reason for something, and the discrepancy had no obvious reason.

questions.questionText: The reply was polite, yet its careful wording suggested that the company was _____ about accepting liability.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reluctant'. 'Reluctant' means unwilling, which careful, guarded wording usually indicates.

questions.questionText: The new employee arrived with strong theoretical knowledge but little _____ exposure to industrial machinery.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'practical'. 'Practical' means relating to real experience, which is contrasted with theory.

questions.questionText: The company's share price fell sharply after the regulator announced a formal _____ into its accounting practices.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'inquiry'. A formal 'inquiry' is an official investigation, which is what a regulator initiates.

questions.questionText: The patient remained _____ throughout the procedure and was able to answer questions.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'conscious'. 'Conscious' means awake and aware, which the ability to answer confirms.

questions.questionText: The engineer was careful to _____ the limits of the simulation when presenting the results to the client.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'acknowledge'. 'Acknowledge' means to admit openly, which honest reporting of model limits involves.

questions.questionText: The new dashboard was praised for being _____; even first-time users could navigate it without training.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'intuitive'. 'Intuitive' means easy to understand and use without instruction, exactly what the second clause describes.

questions.questionText: The scheme encourages small manufacturers to _____ their products so that they can sell in regulated markets.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'certify'. 'Certify' means to obtain official confirmation of standards, which regulated markets require.

questions.questionText: The team decided to _____ the legacy module rather than maintain two versions of the same logic.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'retire'. To 'retire' a module means to withdraw it from use, avoiding duplicated maintenance.

questions.questionText: Because the two offices follow different formats, the data had to be _____ before analysis.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'standardised'. 'Standardised' means brought to a common format, which differing formats require.

questions.questionText: Because the symptoms appeared suddenly, the doctor could not immediately _____ the cause of the illness.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'diagnose'. 'Diagnose' means to identify the nature of an illness, which is what the doctor could not do at once.

questions.questionText: A power failure seemed _____, as the voltage had been fluctuating for over an hour.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'imminent'. 'Imminent' means about to happen; 'eminent' means distinguished.

questions.questionText: The firm's growth strategy proved _____ because it relied entirely on a single large customer.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'risky'. 'Risky' means involving the possibility of loss, which depending on one customer clearly is.

questions.questionText: A short briefing will _____ the main session, after which the groups will separate.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'precede'. 'Precede' means to come before; 'proceed' means to go forward.

questions.questionText: The organisers decided to _____ the seminar to the following month because the main speaker fell ill.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'defer'. 'Defer' means to put off to a later time; 'differ' means to be unlike.

questions.questionText: The _____ department has been asked to verify the qualifications of all new recruits.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'personnel'. 'Personnel' refers to the staff of an organisation; 'personal' means private.

questions.questionText: The chief guest praised the students for an exhibition that was both imaginative and technically _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'sound'. 'Technically sound' means free from technical faults, a standard expression of approval.

questions.questionText: Because the customer complaints kept recurring, the team decided to look for the _____ cause rather than applying quick fixes.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'underlying'. 'Underlying' refers to the deeper, fundamental cause, which is contrasted here with quick fixes.

questions.questionText: Given the limited evidence available, the researcher adopted a _____ tone rather than making a definitive claim.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'cautious'. 'Cautious' reflects care and restraint, which is appropriate when the evidence is limited.

questions.questionText: The committee asked the team to _____ the findings in a single page for the board.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'summarise'. 'Summarise' means to state the main points briefly, which a one-page note requires.

questions.questionText: The policy states that complaints must be acknowledged within one working day and _____ within seven.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'settled'. 'Settled' parallels 'acknowledged' and means brought to a conclusion.

questions.questionText: The scholarship committee looked for applicants who had shown _____ in community service.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'initiative'. 'Initiative' means the willingness to act independently, which such committees value.

questions.questionText: The spokesperson refused to _____ on the ongoing investigation, citing legal advice.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'comment'. 'Comment on' means to express an opinion about something.

questions.questionText: The supervisor warned that repeated absence without notice would _____ disciplinary action.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'invite'. The collocation 'invite disciplinary action' means to bring it upon oneself.

questions.questionText: Because the specification kept changing, the developers found it difficult to _____ a stable design.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'finalise'. 'Finalise' means to settle something conclusively, which constant change prevents.

questions.questionText: The temperature in the furnace must be controlled _____, since even a small variation spoils the alloy.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'precisely'. 'Precisely' means exactly, which the sensitivity of the alloy demands.

questions.questionText: The company published a detailed sustainability report in order to appear more _____ to its investors.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'transparent'. 'Transparent' means open about one's actions, which detailed public reporting demonstrates.

questions.questionText: Before signing the agreement, the legal team was asked to _____ every clause for hidden liabilities.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'scrutinise'. 'Scrutinise' means to examine very closely, which is necessary when searching for hidden liabilities.

questions.questionText: The audit revealed only _____ discrepancies, so the management saw no reason to order a detailed investigation.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'minor'. 'Minor' means small and unimportant, which explains why no detailed investigation was ordered.

questions.questionText: The hostel warden asked the students to _____ from using high-wattage appliances in their rooms.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'refrain'. 'Refrain from' means to stop oneself from doing something, the usual phrasing of such a request.

questions.questionText: The device was recalled after a manufacturing _____ was found in one batch of batteries.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'defect'. 'Defect' means a fault in manufacture, the usual reason for a product recall.

questions.questionText: The report was returned for revision because several of its claims were not _____ by the data presented.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'supported'. 'Supported' means backed up by evidence, which the data failed to provide.

questions.questionText: The team's morale improved noticeably after the manager began to _____ individual contributions in weekly meetings.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'acknowledge'. 'Acknowledge' means to recognise publicly, and such recognition explains the improvement in morale.

questions.questionText: Good documentation helps new members _____ the system without constantly interrupting their colleagues.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'understand'. 'Understand' means to grasp how something works, which documentation supports.

questions.questionText: Rising sea levels are expected to _____ low-lying coastal settlements over the coming decades.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'threaten'. 'Threaten' means to put at risk, which rising seas do to coastal areas.

questions.questionText: The start-up attracted funding because its business model was both novel and _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'scalable'. 'Scalable' means able to grow without a proportionate rise in cost, a key attraction for investors.

questions.questionText: The lecturer paused frequently to _____ difficult concepts with everyday examples.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'illustrate'. 'Illustrate' means to make something clear by giving examples, exactly as described.

questions.questionText: The firewall logs showed a pattern of _____ login attempts from a single foreign address.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'suspicious'. 'Suspicious' means arousing distrust; repeated attempts from one foreign address fit this description.

questions.questionText: Strict norms were introduced to reduce the _____ of particulate matter from brick kilns.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'emission'. 'Emission' means the release of a substance into the air, which is what kilns produce.

questions.questionText: The technician explained that the fault was _____: it appeared only when the machine had been running for several hours.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'intermittent'. 'Intermittent' means occurring at irregular intervals, which the description confirms.

questions.questionText: The chief guest spoke briefly and _____, finishing well within the ten minutes allotted to her.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'concisely'. 'Concisely' means in few words, which matches both 'briefly' and the short time taken.

questions.questionText: The first version of the app crashed frequently. After the rewrite, users reported a _____ improvement in stability.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'marked'. 'Marked' means clearly noticeable, which matches a change from frequent crashes to stability.

questions.questionText: The manager's instructions were so _____ that two team members understood the deadline differently.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'ambiguous'. 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation, which explains the conflicting understanding.

questions.questionText: The paper does not state the figure explicitly, but the data clearly _____ a downward trend.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'imply'. A text or speaker 'implies'; the reader 'infers'.

questions.questionText: Because the two modules were developed independently, they turned out not to be _____ with each other.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'compatible'. 'Compatible' means able to work together, which independently developed modules often are not.

questions.questionText: The report's recommendations were sensible, but they were not accompanied by any _____ plan for putting them into practice.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'concrete'. 'Concrete' here means specific and practical, as opposed to vague suggestions.

questions.questionText: The traffic police introduced a trial one-way system near the market. Shopkeepers protested, saying it had _____ their daily sales.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'hurt'. 'Hurt' means harmed; the protest shows the system reduced sales.

questions.questionText: The warehouse adopted barcode scanning, after which stock discrepancies fell _____ from eleven per cent to under one.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'sharply'. 'Sharply' describes a steep fall, which the figures in the sentence show.

questions.questionText: The recruiter asked her to _____ her salary expectations before the final round.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'state'. 'State' as a verb means to express clearly in speech or writing.

questions.questionText: The two cities have similar populations; their public transport systems, _____, are very different.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'however'. 'However' marks the contrast between similarity in one respect and difference in another.

questions.questionText: The visiting professor paid the team a handsome _____ on the quality of their presentation.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'compliment'. 'Compliment' is an expression of praise, which is what was paid to the team.

questions.questionText: Regular patching helps organisations _____ the risk of a security breach rather than eliminating it entirely.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'mitigate'. 'Mitigate' means to make something less severe; the sentence contrasts reducing risk with removing it completely.

questions.questionText: Working on live projects during the internship helped her _____ practical experience that classroom learning could not provide.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'gain'. The standard collocation is 'gain experience', meaning to acquire it through practice.

questions.questionText: Species that cannot _____ to rising temperatures are likely to disappear from the region.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'adapt'. 'Adapt' means to adjust to new conditions, which is the issue in a warming climate.

questions.questionText: The plant manager attributed the drop in output to a _____ of trained operators rather than to machine failure.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'shortage'. 'Shortage' means an insufficient supply, which explains reduced output.

questions.questionText: The manager wanted to _____ the anxious client that the delivery date would be honoured.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'assure'. 'Assure' means to tell someone confidently to remove their doubt, and it takes a personal object.

questions.questionText: The data entry errors were few but _____, since a single wrong digit changed the entire billing amount.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'consequential'. 'Consequential' means having important results, which fits errors with large effects.

questions.questionText: The volunteers' work was recognised in an _____ message from the district collector.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'appreciative'. 'Appreciative' means expressing gratitude, which recognition of good work involves.

questions.questionText: The report recommends regular drills so that employees can respond _____ in the event of a fire.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'promptly'. 'Promptly' means without delay, which is precisely the purpose of conducting regular drills.

questions.questionText: The customer's complaint was _____ within an hour, which is why she later wrote an appreciative review.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'resolved'. 'Resolved' means settled satisfactorily, which explains the positive review.

questions.questionText: The results of the two trials were nearly identical, which _____ the team's confidence in the method.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'reinforced'. 'Reinforced' means strengthened, the natural effect of consistent results on confidence.

questions.questionText: The audit firm was replaced because its reports were considered insufficiently _____ of the management.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'independent'. 'Independent' means free from influence, which an auditor's reports must be.

questions.questionText: The results of the two laboratories differed _____, which forced the team to recheck the calibration.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'significantly'. 'Significantly' means to an important degree, which justifies rechecking the instruments.

questions.questionText: The flood caused _____ damage to the warehouse; nearly the entire stock had to be written off.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'extensive'. 'Extensive' means covering a large area or amount, consistent with writing off the entire stock.

questions.questionText: Because the ticket system was overloaded, many genuine complaints were _____ for days.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'unattended'. 'Unattended' means not dealt with, the natural result of an overloaded system.

questions.questionText: The entire approach rests on a simple _____: that users will act in their own interest.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'principle'. 'Principle' means a fundamental rule or assumption; 'principal' means chief or a head of institution.

questions.questionText: New employees are expected to _____ to the organisation's code of conduct from their first day.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'conform'. 'Conform to' means to comply with rules or standards.

questions.questionText: Although the two words sound similar, their meanings are entirely _____, and using one for the other changes the sense.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'distinct'. 'Distinct' means clearly different, which the second clause confirms.

questions.questionText: Before the trial run, the operators were asked to _____ themselves with the emergency shutdown procedure.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'acquaint'. 'Acquaint oneself with' means to learn about something, which safety preparation requires.

questions.questionText: The research team worked on the problem for two years before they finally achieved a _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'breakthrough'. A 'breakthrough' is an important discovery after sustained effort.

questions.questionText: Though the new policy was announced with great enthusiasm, its implementation has been _____ so far.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'patchy'. 'Patchy' means inconsistent and incomplete, which contrasts with the enthusiastic announcement.

questions.questionText: The server failed repeatedly because the system could not _____ the sudden surge in user traffic.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'handle'. 'Handle' means to cope with or manage; the system could not manage the surge, so it failed.

questions.questionText: The scheme offers a subsidy to farmers who adopt drip irrigation, as it uses water far more _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'efficiently'. 'Efficiently' means with little waste, which is the recognised advantage of drip irrigation.

questions.questionText: The library installed self-checkout machines. Queues at the counter have since become much _____.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'shorter'. 'Shorter' follows logically from self-service machines reducing counter traffic.

questions.questionText: _____ the heavy workload, the team managed to release the update on the promised date.
questions.explanationText: The correct answer is 'Despite'. 'Despite' introduces a contrast between difficulty and success.
